Three existing records — D0036, D0049 and D0063 — recorded `status: accepted` with no signature beside them, and are set to `blocked-on-owner`, which is what they actually are. The boundary sitting's step 8 is where they become accepted, by signature. | accepted | — | governance-paths | pytest: `tests/test_tier_c_signatures.py`; manifest: `tests/poison/check-decisions-unsigned-tier-c/decisions/0001-poison-tier-c-accepted.yaml` |
| D0065 | A | The boundary-sitting driver gated three steps on a later step's output | scripts/boundary_sitting.sh is corrected in three places, all found by the owner running it. (1) Step 6 installed the new custodian and immediately required it to be green, but that custodian checks governance/custody.sha256 and its owner signature, and both are step 7's work — the custody set hashes scripts/custodian.sh itself, so neither regenerating nor signing can precede the install. (1b) Step 0's precondition `make verify` fails for the same reason on a first sitting, so the driver would refuse to start on the second run for the very condition it was convened to fix. Both now use one helper, unexpected_failures, that tolerates the custodian's custody-set complaints by name and dies on anything else; step 7 signs and then re-runs the custodian as a gate that tolerates none of them. check_manifest's "custody drift" is deliberately NOT tolerated anywhere — that is the channel saying a file the owner signed for changed, and at step 0 it means someone edited a guard outside this driver. (2) add_manifest_rows wrote a manifest row for every file under an installed fixture, including the tag-signer bundle generated at the sitting (conferral ruling 6), which `git mv` had never tracked — so check_manifest failed with "manifest rows must be committed artifacts" (D0034) at step 9, whose own gate is check_manifest. It now stages each file it manifests. The bundle is staged and D0064's binding, which pointed at the fixture's pre-installation path under docs/redteam/fixture-candidates/, is retargeted to its sealed path and upgraded from a file binding to a manifest one. | accepted | — | governance-paths | file: `scripts/boundary_sitting.sh`; manifest: `tests/poison/custodian-tag-signer/repo.bundle` |
| D0066 | A | The sitting driver treated EDITOR and PAGER as command names | scripts/boundary_sitting.sh invoked the owner's editor and pager as `"${EDITOR:-nano}" BRIEF.md` — one quoted word — so an EDITOR holding a command LINE rather than a bare program name failed with `command not found`. The owner's is `emacsclient -nw -a 'emacs -nw'`, which is an ordinary setting, as is a PAGER of `less -FRX`; there were eight such pager call sites and one editor call site. Both now go through one helper each, `edit` and `page`, which use `eval "$EDITOR" '"$@"'` — the same construction git uses, and for the same reason. Dropping the quotes instead would word-split the value, but would also split the owner's own quoting apart, so `-a 'emacs -nw'` would arrive as two arguments. Separately, step 4b put "Keep this edit?" to the owner after the editor failed to run, over an empty diff; it now checks `git diff --quiet` first and says plainly that the amendment has not landed, naming the draft to apply and noting the step returns on the next run. | accepted | — | governance-paths | file: `scripts/boundary_sitting.sh` |
| D0067 | A | Two sitting loops read the owner's answer from the list they were iterating | Three loops in scripts/boundary_sitting.sh were written `while IFS= read -r rec; do … done < <(ls -1 decisions/*.yaml | sort)`. That redirection applies to the whole compound command, so every `read` in the body — including the one inside confirm() — takes its input from the file list rather than from the keyboard. Two of the three contain the confirm that decides whether a Tier-C record is signed: sign_tier_c_records (step 1, and again at the end of step 8) and step 8's own queue loop. All three are replaced by `mapfile -t` into an array followed by a plain `for`, which leaves stdin alone; add_manifest_rows is converted with them although it asks nothing today, because the difference between the two spellings is invisible until the day someone adds a prompt. | accepted | — | governance-paths | file: `scripts/boundary_sitting.sh`; file: `scripts/rehearse_sitting.sh` |
| D0068 | A | The boundary-sitting driver is rehearsed end to end before it touches the owner's key | scripts/rehearse_sitting.sh executes scripts/boundary_sitting.sh from end to end with no human present: a disposable clone of this repo, a throwaway ed25519 key appended to allowed_signers as a second owner@tannen principal, every prompt answered from a file, a non-interactive stand-in for $EDITOR that applies the drafted BRIEF blocks, and eleven assertions about what a completed sitting must leave behind — the close tag signed and verifying, the custody set signed, a fresh signed receipt, the custodian green with no tolerances, `make verify` green, nothing uncommitted, and no Tier-C door left unsigned. Three paths are rehearsed: `--from worktree` (HEAD plus uncommitted work — what the owner is about to run, and the one that must be green), `--from head` (the sitting from a pristine repo), and `--answers n` (the owner declines everything). Its only access to the real repository is `git clone` and a read-only diff. . Three defects it found in its first four runs are fixed with it. (1) The prompt loops, recorded separately as D0067. (2) `.verify-evidence/` — the scratch store `make verify` builds to satisfy RT-05 — was untracked and unignored, and a red gate leaves it behind, so the sitting's `git add -A` would have committed it; it is now in .gitignore. (3) A decision binding that names a fixture-candidate path stops resolving the moment step 5 installs the fixture, and nothing surfaced that until step 9, five signatures later; step 5 now checks for exactly the two messages a file move produces and stops there, where being wrong costs a builder retargeting a binding rather than an owner having signed over a red gate. In the same pass the driver's four `uv run python` invocations became `.venv/bin/python -I -P`, the spelling the Makefile already uses: a script that drives the owner's key should not resolve its interpreter through pyproject.toml and uv.lock, which are the builder's to edit (RT-02, conferral ruling 3, D0063). | accepted | — | governance-paths | file: `scripts/rehearse_sitting.sh`; file: `scripts/boundary_sitting.sh`; file: `.gitignore` |
| D0069 | A | The sitting spent its longest minute in silence and read as hung | Step 0 of scripts/boundary_sitting.sh ran the gate as `verify_out=$(make verify 2>&1)` and printed the captured output afterwards, so the driver's first question was followed by roughly fifty seconds of a completely still terminal — 174 tests, ten law suites and a batched pytest run inside check_decisions, none of it visible. The owner read that as a hang and killed the sitting twice before it reached step 1. It now streams through `tee` into a temporary log and reads PIPESTATUS on the following line; the log is what unexpected_failures parses, so nothing about the tolerance logic changes. Capturing output and displaying it are two acts and `$( )` performs only the first. . Where the capture came from is the part worth recording. Step 0 streamed the gate when the driver was written (D0062). It was changed to capture by the fix for D0065, which needed the gate's text in order to tell the two tolerated custody-set failures from a genuinely red gate — and took that text the obvious way, by substitution, silently trading the owner's view of the run for the script's. Fixing a real defect introduced this one in the same edit, which is the argument for the harness check below rather than for more care. . The convention that replaces the patch: a step about to be quiet for more than a moment announces it first, through a `waiting()` helper rather than an ordinary note, stating the expected duration. Three sites use it — the step-0 gate (~1 minute, measured), the step-5 binding check (~15s), and the step-6 custodian run (~5s). The duration is measured on this machine and written down rather than guessed; being wrong by a minute is fine, being absent is not, because an unbounded wait with no output cannot be told from a hang. . scripts/rehearse_sitting.sh enforces the convention. It now writes a second transcript with the elapsed second on every line, and fails if any gap longer than 25 seconds is not preceded by a `[waiting]` line, printing the offending silences with the line that came before each. A new TANNEN_REHEARSE_DRIVER environment variable overlays a driver from somewhere other than the working tree, which is how this check was watched catching the defect that motivated it: reconstruct the pre-fix step 0 in a copy of the driver, point the variable at that copy, and the new check reports `50s of silence` where the owner sat looking at nothing, while the fixed driver in the same harness passes. | accepted | — | governance-paths | file: `scripts/boundary_sitting.sh`; file: `scripts/rehearse_sitting.sh` |
